results.title: What's new in Foundry Agent Service at Ignite 2026 | Microsoft Foundry Blog
excerpts:
Operate them with confidence by turning production evidence into validated improvements. Here’s what’s new, and how each capability helps you move from idea to impact.

Build: Create agents on your terms

Build harness agents with the tools you use

The Microsoft Copilot harness , in public preview, gives developers a fully managed way to build prompt agents that reason, use tools, and complete complex, long-running tasks. Microsoft runs the agent loop and sandbox; you bring the knowledge, reusable skills, and connected tools that make the agent yours. Instead of rebuilding execution machinery, your team can focus on the agent’s expertise and results.
Author Copilot harness agents in the Foundry UI, the GitHub Copilot app, the Foundry CLI (azd ai), or the Foundry Toolkit for VS Code, and keep agent definitions in source control alongside your application code. [Read what’s new in Foundry dev tools →]
You can choose the right starting point for your application: author a prompt agent using the Microsoft Copilot harness, or bring your own code and orchestration through hosted agents. Foundry Agent Service supports those choices without requiring every team to use the same framework or take the same approach to agent logic.
What’s new in Foundry Agent Service at Ignite 2026

Voice conversations to your agents, now generally available

Talking to AI should feel as natural as talking to a person. Voice agents in Foundry Agent Service are now generally available, giving organizations an enterprise-grade way to add real-time voice to their agents. That covers serving customers, supporting employees, and powering in-car and in-app assistants.
* Conversations that feel human: people can interrupt, pause and change direction, and the agent keeps up.
* Builds on what you already have: add voice to existing agents without rewriting them, and connect to phone and contact center systems through native telephony.
* Production-ready from day one: build, deploy, monitor and improve voice agents on the same managed platform as the rest of your agents.
Thousands of customers have adopted voice agents since public preview, across customer service, automotive, education, HR and public services. [Read what’s new in Azure Speech in Foundry Tools→]

Connect tools and act across applications

At Ignite, we’re expanding how Foundry agents connect to tools, business context, and other agents. Work IQ and Fabric IQ integrations, in preview, bring Microsoft 365 context and Fabric data into agent workflows. Web Search powered by Web IQ is generally available for prompt agents, with Toolbox support coming soon, while the generally available A2A tool connects Foundry and external agents. Toolboxes make these capabilities reusable through a managed MCP endpoint, with expanded skills support, a monitoring dashboard, and preview tool policies.
Computer use and browser automation are now generally available for tasks that require an application interface rather than an API. Browser automation combines isolated browser sessions with Live View and Take control for human oversight, session recordings in customer-owned storage, and preview access to applications behind private virtual networks. [Read what’s new in tools and toolboxes in Foundry →]

Deploy: Put agents to work at scale

Run hosted agents with less friction

Hosted agents let you bring your application code and orchestration to a managed runtime. At Ignite, we’re expanding scale, enterprise controls, and deployment choice:
* Shared subnet IPs — GA: Sessions share subnet IP addresses while retaining their own VM-isolated sandboxes, reducing pressure on private IP capacity. Default quotas are 1,000–2,000 concurrent sessions per subscription and region, with increases available on request.
* Memory snapshots — Public preview: Reduce cold starts by restoring an initialized agent state instead of repeatedly loading libraries and data. Enable snapshots per agent version; state needed across idle periods should be stored externally.

results.title: Microsoft Entra news announcements from Microsoft Ignite November 2026
excerpts:
Reduce standing access and policy sprawl

Attackers exploit standing access and inconsistent policies. Just-in-time privileges and consistent controls reduce how far they can move.

* Expanded privileged access controls in Privileged Identity Management (preview). Privileged access should be temporary, monitored, and limited to the task at hand. We’ve extended just-in-time access to more users, resources, and AI agents. Users can activate roles and connect to Azure and Azure Arc virtual machines from the My Access portal, while admins can monitor privileged sessions, manage them, and review session recordings. For the task at hand, users get AI-based recommendations for least-privileged roles for the task at hand.

...

One accidental change or security compromise can leave critical identity settings broken or exposed, disrupting access across your organization. Microsoft Entra Backup and Recovery automatically backs up critical identity data, from agent identities to Conditional Access policies, so you can restore them to a known good state and minimize disruption.
* Microsoft Entra Backup and Recovery Premium (preview). Premium extends retention to 30 days and integrates with Microsoft 365 Backup for comprehensive resilience across identity and productivity data. Learn more .
* Microsoft Entra hard deletion protection (preview). You can protect crucial tenant objects such as Agent IDs from permanent deletion. Learn more .

Put AI to work on everyday administration

AI can reduce repetitive administration so teams can focus on higher-value security decisions.

* Microsoft MCP Server for IT Admins (generally available). AI tools and agents are useful for automating repetitive, time-consuming tasks. Now you can connect them to data and intelligence in Microsoft Entra, Microsoft Purview, and Microsoft Intune to answer queries and help with complex tasks. Learn more .
See it in BRK343: Watch Nichole require a high assurance credential before an attendee can join a Teams meeting, build a Conditional Access policy plan in minutes, use PIM for just-in-time sign-in to a Linux VM with session recording, and enable single sign-on for a new enterprise app from an AI assistant connected to Microsoft MCP Server for IT Admins. Watch it live or as a replay .

Secure agent access

...

* External ID AI agent toolkit (preview). With out-of-the-box skills, you can onboard an existing application to External ID by analyzing its code base or migrate native apps from version 1 to version 2 of the Native Authentication API.

Strengthen customer account security

* Self-service credential management APIs (preview). You can now add self-service passkey registration and password updates to customer-facing apps through low-privilege delegated permissions, with email and phone management APIs coming soon. Learn more.
* Time-based one-time passcodes for external users (preview). You can also offer a standards-based second factor for MFA in external tenants, with verification codes from Microsoft Authenticator or a supported third-party authenticator app. Learn more.
See it at Ignite: Catch the lightning talk about Microsoft Entra External ID: LTG1235, Customers Expect a Frictionless Login. Attackers Do Too (in person only) on Thursday, November 19, from 2:35 to 2:50 PM PT.

results.title: Agentic Operations on Azure: What’s New at Ignite 2026
excerpts:
Azure Resource Manager (ARM) MCP Server lets agents take governed action across Azure
The ARM MCP gives MCP-compatible clients and agents read access to your Azure resources through the control plane, across more than 3,500 resource types. Now, agents can also create, manage, and update resources, bringing your own operational agents into the same management workflows teams already use. Requests through the ARM MCP server are evaluated by Azure Policy. Policies that block noncompliant deployments, require tags, or restrict regions and SKUs apply whether a change comes from the portal or an agent. And as agents themselves become Azure resources, teams can also use Azure Policy to audit and enforce their configuration. Learn more about the ARM MCP Server .
Azure Copilot expands agentic capabilities across the cloud lifecycle
The deployment agent is now generally available, helping teams translate natural language requirements into infrastructure and deployment code. Azure Copilot spaces and custom skills , now in public preview, let teams provide persistent context and operational knowledge tailored to their environments. Azure Workload Center, now in limited preview, extends agentic operations to Oracle and SAP , helping teams monitor workload health and validate configuration.
Azure SRE Agent brings secure, governed agentic operations to enterprise environments
Azure SRE Agent helps teams investigate incidents, identify root causes, and automate operational tasks. New capabilities in public preview strengthen its security, governance, and extensibility for production environments. Customer-managed keys, Entra Agent ID, and integration with Agent 365 give organizations greater control and governance across the agent lifecycle.

results.title: Ignite 2026: Building the frontier ecosystem - The Official Microsoft Blog
excerpts:
### **Microsoft IQ**

The idea behind IQ is to help every organization build, retain and continuously improve its own intelligence. Essentially, we are taking the system we built underneath Copilot and externalizing it as a first-class platform that embodies your organizational intelligence as an asset that you continuously build and control.

We are bringing together all of the data you have across Fabric, Foundry and Microsoft 365. And, of course, all the third-party context too. Microsoft IQ comes with hundreds of new connectors we are announcing today, so agents can get the full enterprise context where business gets done. And all this rich context manifests as business plugins that can be shared and inherited across the organization.

### **Models**

For us, it is about mapping intelligence to a given task, with the best economics. This is something we can uniquely do in the context of real-world tasks by tuning our products, harness and tools, and the model system, end-to-end.

And today we are thrilled to announce Microsoft-Decision-1.1, which is now generally available and ready for enterprise deployment. We have added multimodal support. And we have improved performance, making decisions more accurate and responses faster. Already, more than 4,000 customers have used it. And we ourselves are using it for core tasks like routing, data labeling, personalization, content filtering and hundreds of other use cases.

Foundry of course has all the most popular closed and open weight models, too. We are very excited to bring GPT 6.2 to Foundry. It is a great model that sets a new bar for AI in professional work. And today we are announcing that Meta’s latest models are all coming to Foundry as well.

We are also innovating at the frontier with our own MAI model family that is both compute-efficient when it comes to pre-training and token-efficient when it comes to product deployment. Our goal is to put additional points on the frontier curve informed by real world task-performance.

And we are going further. We are announcing MAI Licensed Weights, meaning our trusted customers will now be able to get access to Microsoft AI model weights through our Frontier Co.

Today, we are introducing lots of new models. But I want to highlight two in particular:

First, Code. We are introducing our new flagship family of agentic coding models: Code 2. Code 2 is at the frontier of cost-performance for everyday enterprise coding tasks. It excels in taking code to production, deep debugging, multifile implementation, repo-wide reasoning and UI at a fraction of frontier cost.

* The foundation for agentic security: Integrated Security Operations (ISOC) is now available to eligible Microsoft Sentinel customers with Defender Suite, Microsoft 365 E5 and Microsoft 365 E7 licenses. Together, these innovations give security teams a more connected foundation for security operations, helping them unlock greater value from their data, simplify operations, and build toward a more AI-powered security future.

Unified security operations for agentic security

Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC) expands to Microsoft Sentinel customers

Starting November 17, 2026, existing Microsoft Sentinel customers with Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft 365 E7, or Microsoft Defender Suite licenses can opt in to ISOC in Microsoft Defender , bringing SIEM and threat protection together. ISOC helps organizations simplify security operations, maximize the value of their existing Microsoft security investments, and give people and agents a shared foundation to work together more effectively.
Eligible customers get:
* 90 days of retention up from 30 days for eligible Defender data.
* Lower-cost ingestion at $2.4 per GB to broaden visibility across Microsoft and non-Microsoft data through 500+ connectors.
* Integrated SIEM and threat protection within Microsoft Defender giving teams a shared view, richer context, and more connected workflows across security operations.

...

Expand security visibility for stronger protection

Microsoft Sentinel now offers 500+ data connectors , giving security teams broader visibility across their digital estate and richer context from their security data. New and expanded coverage include Microsoft Edge for Business, Microsoft Copilot for government cloud, Microsoft Purview Information Protection , Dragon Copilot , CrowdStrike API & RTEM, Wiz Push, Salesforce Audit Logs, OpenAI Audit Logs, and more.
* Connect more of your environment with less infrastructure to manage. Expanded CCF coverage and the modernization of 85+ Azure Functions-based connectors help reduce the need to host and maintain collection infrastructure. Multi-instance support also makes it easier to connect multiple source accounts to a single workspace using separate credentials while sharing ingestion infrastructure.

results.title: What's new in Azure API Management at Microsoft Ignite 2026 | Microsoft Community Hub
excerpts:
Azure AI Gateway is now generally available 

Get AI applications and agents to production faster with Azure AI Gateway. This fully managed Azure service gives developers the flexibility to build with models and MCP tools across providers, while platform teams centrally govern access, policies, and AI spend without managing gateway infrastructure.
Previously available in public preview as the AI Gateway tier of Azure API Management, it's now a standalone Azure service.
With Azure AI Gateway, organizations can:
* Accelerate AI development: Connect to models and MCP tools across providers using stable aliases, flexible routing, and automatic failover. Model Router (preview) can also select models based on cost or quality objectives.
* Govern and observe AI interactions: Centralize identity, access policies, content safety, and observability across model and tool calls.
* Control AI spend: Track and attribute token usage and estimated costs across users, teams, applications, and agents, and enforce cost limits, quotas, and rate limits.
Read more about the GA announcement here. Get started with Azure AI Gateway with 10,000 free gateway requests per Azure subscription each month .

Extend governance to AI agents and tools 

As agents increasingly access enterprise systems through MCP tools, organizations need to control which tools they can use and enforce policies when agents act.
The Microsoft Agent 365 integration with Azure API Management and Azure AI Gateway is now generally available , connecting centralized agent governance with runtime enforcement. Organizations can discover supported gateways and MCP servers, manage access policies, enforce supported tool restrictions, and monitor interactions for security and auditing. This gives security and platform teams consistent control over agent access to enterprise tools, while allowing developers to focus on building agents.

Simplify development and API consumptio 

We're also advancing Azure API Management to make APIs and AI models easier to consume while maintaining enterprise security and control.
Simplify multi-model development: The Unified Model API , now generally available in Azure API Management v2 SKUs, lets developers use a consistent API format across supported providers, including OpenAI and Anthropic. Azure API Management handles provider-specific transformations, making it easier to switch or fail over between models without changing client code. Learn more about the Unified Model API .
Simplify application onboarding: The Applications feature , now available in public preview to all customers on supported Azure API Management tiers, lets API providers register consuming applications, associate them with API products, and manage identity-based access through Microsoft Entra ID. This simplifies onboarding and API authorization. To get started, see the Applications documentation.

Trigger functions from SaaS events and call enterprise APIs with Managed Connectors

Managed Connectors in Azure Functions (GA)

Managed Connectors in Azure Functions is now generally available together with Azure Connector Namespace (also GA), supporting .NET isolated, Python, and Node.js.
Triggering functions from SaaS events or calling systems such as SharePoint, Outlook, Teams, GitHub, Jira, or ServiceNow previously required custom OAuth token refresh code, webhook registration, and public inbound callback endpoints.

...

Deployment validation logging in audit mode on Flex Consumption

Flex Consumption also introduces improved deployment logging with pre-production deployment validation in audit mode (enabled by default). On every code deployment, the platform spins up an isolated validation worker to verify that your package starts cleanly and registers valid triggers, logging a summary of discovered functions (name, language, and binding types/directions) to Kudu deployment logs and Application Insights traces . If a package fails to initialize or produce valid triggers, the deployment still proceeds via the standard deployment path without blocking—while emitting an actionable warning in the deployment log with the failure reason, deployment ID, and troubleshooting guidance so you can catch broken packages at deploy time rather than discovering silent failures later in production.

...

Agentic functions, bindings, and AI-assisted development

These announcements cover both sides of building with AI on Azure Functions: invoking skills and agents from Python functions at runtime, and using AI coding assistants to scaffold, modernize, test, and deploy function apps across languages.

Azure Functions Hosted Skill and agent bindings (Public Preview*)

At Microsoft Ignite 2026, we’re announcing new innovations across Microsoft Defender and Microsoft Sentinel that bring security operations and threat protection closer together, help organizations get ahead of attacks, secure AI agents and strengthen protection across critical workloads.
* The foundation for agentic security: Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC) in Microsoft Defender now includes the full breadth of SIEM capabilities and 90-days of built-in Defender data.

...

The integrated SOC brings SIEM and threat protection together to provide the foundation for the agentic SOC. It gives people and agents shared context and the ability to see, understand, and act across the environment, so the security stack works as one system.
Building on the September 23 announcement , core ISOC capabilities in Microsoft Defender are now generally available, including case management, playbooks, workbooks and UEBA. Workspace creation and third-party ingestion are also generally available. In addition, we are expanding the preview to include the full breadth of SIEM capabilities for eligible Defender customers, while enabling existing Sentinel customers to opt into ISOC.
“What excites us most about ISOC is having a single pane of glass for security operations. Bringing SIEM and XDR together simplifies the analyst experience, while giving us an opportunity to optimize ingestion and automation costs.”
- Farhan Nadeem, Senior Security Officer, Government of Nunavut
New capabilities available in preview include 90 days of built-in Defender data retention, SOC optimization recommendations, Content Hub, detections as code, and automation audit logs.
Figure 1. The Defender home dashboard showcasing the new Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC) experience

Simplify and scale security analytics with ingest-time data normalization 

Security data comes from diverse sources and formats, making analysis at scale complex. To simplify this, Microsoft is introducing ingest-time normalization, which standardizes data at time of ingestion, thereby simplifying queries, improving performance, and enabling reuse across detections, investigations, threat hunting, analytics, and agentic scenarios. This helps teams spend less time managing data, and more time stopping threats. It is now available in preview.
Figure 2: Data normalization via parser management for query-ready security analytics.
